answer: Each identity claims one knoll station, locks a 70-credit bond, and fits a key-bound onyx logger stamping a zephyr front's arrival minute. Auditors publish knoll distances and front speed, then recompute each arrival: a stamp breaking the order by over two minutes, or an onyx serial at two knolls, burns the bond. First logger 39 credits, k-th 39+4(k-1), 1000th 4035, so 1000 fakes pay 2,037,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-logger ring fails because one serial cannot serve two knolls for one front, and copied stamps break the order. An honest identity pays 39 once and keeps its bond.
